facts.t: NITI Aayog cannot allocate a single rupee
facts.d: The Planning Commission approved state plans and controlled plan transfers. Its successor has no financial powers at all — it advises. That single difference is the root of nearly every criticism levelled at it.

facts.t: Neither body was ever created by law
facts.d: The Planning Commission was set up by a Cabinet resolution in 1950 and NITI Aayog by another in 2015. Neither has ever had a statute or a constitutional basis — unlike the Finance Commission, which sits in Article 280.

facts.t: Atal Tinkering Labs put fabrication tools in school corridors
facts.d: Under the Atal Innovation Mission, thousands of schools received 3D printers, sensors and robotics kits. It is one of the few NITI Aayog programmes that operates directly at the level of individual institutions rather than through state governments.

bank.e: 2015, replacing the Planning Commission that had functioned since 1950.

bank.q: Comparing NITI Aayog with the Planning Commission, consider the following statements:
s: NITI Aayog has no power to allocate funds to states.
It was created by a constitutional amendment.
It emphasises cooperative and competitive federalism rather than top-down planning.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. It was created by an executive resolution, not by amendment or statute — a recurring criticism.

bank.q: Match List I (case study) with List II (sector and state):
pairs: 1. Nutrition delivery through women's self-help groups in Odisha
2. Rainwater harvesting for well recharge in Kerala
3. Real-time app monitoring of child health in Gujarat
bank.e: Mazhapolima is Kerala's well-recharge programme, Panchayat Banks are Jharkhand's village banking model, decentralised ICDS is Odisha's SHG-run nutrition scheme, and SMART Anganwadi is Gujarat's monitoring app.

bank.q: Which one of the following is NOT a challenge identified for NITI Aayog?
bank.e: The opposite is the criticism — it has no statutory authority at all, which is why commentators call for financial and legislative teeth.

bank.as: NITI Aayog is described as needing to evolve from a think tank into a do tank.
bank.rs: Its advisory role combined with weak accountability limits its ability to drive change.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion — a vision without velocity, in the phrase used to summarise the problem.

bank.q: The Aspirational Districts Programme is built on which three principles?
bank.e: Convergence of schemes, collaboration between levels of government, and competition among districts through ranked delta indicators.

bank.q: With reference to the Atal Innovation Mission, consider the following:
s: It supports Atal Tinkering Labs in schools.
It supports Atal Incubation Centres for startups.
It provides direct grants to state governments for infrastructure.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. NITI Aayog makes no fund allocations to states — infrastructure grants are not part of its remit.

bank.q: All of the following are proposed reforms for NITI Aayog EXCEPT:
o: Granting it financial and statutory authority
Restoring approval powers over annual state plans
Institutionalising consultation with states and civil society
bank.e: Restoring plan-approval power would recreate the Planning Commission, which is the model the reforms deliberately moved away from. The proposals seek authority within a cooperative framework, not a return to top-down approval.

bank.q: Strategy for New India @75 set out a roadmap across:
Consider the following statements about the rationale for NITI Aayog:
s: Decentralised, bottom-up planning suited to India's diversity.
States as active partners rather than recipients of plans.
Direct implementation of centrally sponsored schemes.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. NITI Aayog does not implement schemes — it functions as a think tank and coordinating platform.
